title: What If We Stopped Adding Leap Days?

scenes.text: What if the world stopped adding leap days? The calendar would slowly stop matching the seasons.
A year is really about 365 and a quarter days. Leap days quietly catch up the missing six hours.
Skip them, and the calendar falls behind by about 24 days every century.
After just one century, spring would start in April instead of March.
After about 700 years, January would land in what used to be summer.
Even the century rule exists to fix one last tiny error. Our calendar is a patch on the sky.

description:
